notes: §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR11: "If neither an at end nor an invalid key condition occurs during the execution of a READ statement, the AT END phrase or the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified", then a. "The file position indicator is set and the I-O status associated with file-name-1 is updated", b. for any other exception "control is transferred according to rules of the USE statement following the execution of any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1", c. otherwise the record is made available, the INTO move runs and "Control is transferred to the end of the READ statement or to imperative-statement-2, if specified". KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead renders exactly these branches on the status class: the AT END statements only for a 1x status and the INVALID KEY statements only for 2x, so both are skipped on success and on any other failure; on a 0x status EmitRecordAreaStore fills the record area, then the bound INTO move and the NOT AT END or NOT INVALID KEY statements run (EmitNotPhrase); every statement stores the FILE STATUS item and calls EmitUseHook, whose __IoCheck (EmitUseMachinery, EmitScopeTiers) runs the file-name or open-mode USE procedure for an unsuccessful status no phrase covers and returns to the statement after the READ. IndexedConnector.ReadSequential and ReadRandom set the file position indicator to the key of the record made available and end in FileConnector.ReadSucceeded. The 2023 proviso the change record turns on (the indicator is not set on a record operation conflict) is unreachable at 85: LOCK MODE, SHARING and the READ lock phrases are refused there (COBOL0900), so no record lock exists. Probed at --std 85: a READ NEXT answering 02 runs NOT AT END and its INTO move; READs answering 46 and 47 run the applicable USE procedure and neither AT END, INVALID KEY nor their NOT phrases; an open-mode USE procedure is not run for a file that is not open in that mode. The witness covers a random READ INTO with NOT INVALID KEY, a READ NEXT with NOT AT END, and a 47 that runs only the USE procedure. The status value itself is §1985:IX.1.3.4's: a random READ on an alternate key with duplicates answers 00 where that clause gives 02 (kb/Work PB5117), which is that rule's finding, not this one's.

next.reason: CHANGED on item a alone (family ruling, difference 2). 1985: 'The file position indicator is set and the I-O status associated with file-name-1 is updated' (§1985:IX.4.5.4 GR11) for every READ the rule covers, and after an unsuccessful one 'the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid next record has been established' (§1985:IX.4.5.4 GR12). 2023: 'The I-O status associated with file-name-1 is updated and, if the record operation conflict condition did not occur, the file position indicator is set' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR13), and for that condition 'The file position indicator is unchanged' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR10). The words that differ are 'if the record operation conflict condition did not occur': a case removed from the 1985 result. A program with no post-1985 syntax reaches it: with no SHARING phrase or clause 'the implementor shall define the sharing mode that is established for each file connector' (§2023:14.9.27.4 GR23); with no LOCK MODE clause 'the type of record locking for that opening of a shared file associated with that file connector is defined by the implementor' (§2023:12.4.5.9.4 GR1); and when 'the record identified for access is locked by another file connector', 'the record operation conflict condition exists' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR9). A KEPT that rests on the proviso reaching only locking syntax 1985 cannot write is refuted by those three rules. The opening and items b and c are carried and are no ground. Opening: 'If neither an at end nor an invalid key condition occurs during the execution of a READ statement, the AT END phrase or the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified' in both (§1985:IX.4.5.4 GR11; §2023:14.9.30.4 GR13), and for a statement with INVALID KEY 'the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified' (§2023:9.1.14). b: 1985 'control is transferred according to rules of the USE statement following the execution of any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1'; 2023 'control is transferred according to the rules in 9.1.12, Input-output exception processing. If the exception condition is not a fatal exception condition, control is then transferred to the end of the READ statement' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR13), 9.1.12 naming the USE declarative (§2023:9.1.12 GR2), which runs 'upon the unsuccessful execution of an input-output operation' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR6) and returns 'to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR7). The fatal wording is no change: 1985 already says 'If the I-O status value does indicate a critical error, the implementor determines what action is taken' and otherwise 'returns control to the next executable statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception' (§1985:IX.4.8.4 GR6). c: the record is made available and 1985's 'Control is transferred to the end of the READ statement or to imperative-statement-2, if specified' is 2023's 'if the NOT AT END phrase or NOT INVALID KEY phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR13). For the random READ §2023:9.1.14 restates b and c: 'If the I-O status indicates an unsuccessful completion that is not an invalid key condition, control is transferred according to the rules of any applicable exception processing statements', and on success control goes 'to the imperative-statement specified in the NOT INVALID KEY phrase'. Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993) reworded b only. This text is identical in VIII.4.5.4 GR11 and IX.4.5.4 GR11, so the two records take the same kind and the same 'to'.
